Arrests of immigrant parents create mental health crisis for children

An estimated hundreds of thousands of children, many of them U.S. citi

One detail underscores the policy. Most of these parents have no criminal conviction. I have written about how this enforcement machine expanded across both parties, which is the context this crisis sits inside:

austinkocher.substack.com/p/…

DHS says ICE does not separate families and that parents can designate a safe caregiver. A report by the Women's Refugee Commission and Physicians for Human Rights found many parents are never given that choice.

The harm is measurable. Losing a primary caregiver raises a child's risk of depression, anxiety, PTSD, and developmental delays, and is linked to higher rates of heart disease and diabetes later in life.

Many of these arrests happen at routine ICE check-ins, the appointments families are told to attend. Parents have also been taken while dropping kids at school and inside their homes. Most people detained have no criminal conviction.

The scale is staggering. A Brookings analysis estimates that more than 200,000 children, including 145,000 US citizens, have likely had at least one parent detained since January. About a third of them are under age 6.
